USA: The US faces elevated inflation at 4.2% for 2026 (OECD) versus Fed projections of 2.7%, driven by tariff effects and energy price spikes from Middle East conflict. Core PCE inflation hit 3.1% in January 2026, with Q4 2025 GDP revised down to just 0.7% growth. The Fed is expected to hold rates steady through 2026 after three cuts in late 2025, with some officials discussing potential rate hikes later this year.
CAN: Canada's economy lost momentum in Q2 2025 with falling exports and softer business investment, though unexpected Q3 rebound occurred. Trade-related pressures and uncertainty continue to cloud the near-term outlook, with real GDP growth projected to remain restrained despite recent monetary policy easing and federal initiatives providing some support.
GBR: The UK economy is forecast to grow 1.3% in 2026 according to Goldman Sachs, with the Bank of England expected to cut rates quarterly to reach 3% by Q3 2026. Wage growth has slowed to near the 3% sustainable rate consistent with inflation targets, providing room for monetary easing as inflation moderates.
JPN: Japan's economy shows resilience despite US trade policy uncertainty, with 0.4% real GDP growth expected in 2026 (down from 1.1% in 2025). The economy reached 0.3% excess-demand status in Q2 2025 for the first time since 2019, suggesting sustainable price increases after 30 years of deflation. USD/JPY strength near 158-160 intervention zone raises concerns.
DEU: Germany is benefiting from sharp increases in federal government spending as part of fiscal stimulus measures. The eurozone (including new member Bulgaria in 2026) expects 1.2% average GDP growth in 2026, with German budgetary stimulus driving stronger growth expectations since Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
FRA: French economic growth expected to recover moderately to 0.9% in 2026 from 0.7% in 2025, according to Banque de France. The subdued trajectory mirrors broader global slowdown, with 2025 growth heavily relying on inventory rebuilding in the aeronautics sector, while sustainable momentum from other drivers should emerge in 2026.
ITA: Italy faces ongoing challenges from elevated energy costs and trade tensions. The eurozone inflation has stabilized near 2% target, supported by lower energy costs and easing supply constraints, though the country continues to experience below-trend growth alongside other major European economies.
CHN: China's growth projected at 4.5% in 2026 (Deloitte) to 4.8% (Goldman Sachs) with more expansionary fiscal policy expected. Strong exports outweigh sluggish domestic demand, while inflation remains subdued at 0.6% due to weak domestic demand and overcapacity. US tariff exemptions and policy bank lending provide support despite housing sector weakness.
IND: India faces upward pressure from food prices but overall inflation expected to remain within central bank target range. Growth in South Asia projected to moderate to 6.2% in 2026, mainly reflecting impact of increased trade restrictions, though the country leads GDP growth among emerging economies with rapid technology adoption.
ZAF: South Africa's real GDP growth expected to firm from 1.0% in 2025 to 1.2% in 2026, supported by infrastructure and energy reforms. Sub-Saharan Africa shows resilience with positive but uneven growth, supported by reforms and sector diversification, though growth remains insufficient for job creation needs.
BRA: Brazil saw the largest IMF downgrade of 0.3 percentage points for 2026 growth projections. Inflation remains elevated at 4-6% due to currency weakness, rising labor costs and indexation, though expected to gradually return to target ranges by late 2026. Central bank maintains restrictive policy with 300bps of rate cuts anticipated in 2026.
RUS: Russia continues to face ongoing impacts from the war in Ukraine, with elevated energy prices and sanctions affecting manufacturing. The conflict creates high uncertainty for global markets through energy supply disruptions, though higher oil output and resilient domestic demand provide some economic support in the MENA region context.
